observation.visible_scene: A top-down close view of an open golden/brass kettle with a black-gripped overhead handle, resting on crinkled aluminium foil on a stovetop. To the left is a metal gas-hob grate with a black knob; to the right and behind are white tiled walls, a small brown fruit-like object on the counter, and a blue bowl of white rice in the upper-right corner. Inside the kettle, a dark reddish-brown liquid is at a rolling boil, with continuous bubbling, surface churning and rising steam visible throughout the segment.
visible_changes: The liquid boils continuously across all frames: bubbles form, burst and steam plumes drift upward, with the surface turbulence shifting from frame to frame (ongoing process, not an onset).

A fingertip/hand briefly appears at the bottom edge near the kettle's spout in the early-to-mid frames (around t=0.2–0.6 s) and again near the end (around t=2.2 s), then withdraws; the kettle itself does not move.

A yellowish-green solid mass (likely a piece of vegetable/leaf or bag) becomes visible at the left rim of the liquid in the latter half of the clip (from about t=1.3 s onward) as the churning contents bring it into view; it was not seen in the earlier frames.
The kettle, foil, background objects and framing remain stationary; the only motion is internal to the boiling liquid plus the intermittent hand.
Steam density and bubble pattern fluctuate but the overall vigorous boil persists without stopping.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the liquid is (tea, broth, etc.) and what the green object is.
Whether the hand is steadying the kettle, adding something, or merely resting; no clear contact action is shown.
The start and end of the boiling process, since both clip boundaries fall mid-boil.
uncertain_details: Exact identity of the green object and whether it moved or simply rotated/emerged into view.
Whether any slight frame jitter is camera motion or hand tremor; the scene is essentially static.
Precise timing of the hand's appearance/disappearance due to it being partly cut off at the bottom edge.
